sections.title: Valuation Insights
sections.text: Visa’s consolidated net revenue is reported in [[V.fact.revenue]] and reflects the full‑company scope defined in the filing. The GAAP diluted earnings per share pertains to Class A common stock as shown by [[V.fact.diluted_eps]]. Capital expenditures, recorded in [[V.fact.capex]], cover purchases of property, equipment and technology. The annual metrics follow the fiscal year as defined in the filing, while the latest quarter data are for the three‑month period ending in the most recent quarter. The price used for valuation is the close on the date of the release from [[V.price]], unadjusted for splits or dividends. Operating profitability is strong, with an operating margin of [[V.ratio.operating_margin]] percent, indicating efficient cost management. Return on average equity stands at [[V.ratio.return_on_average_equity]] percent, underscoring high returns to shareholders. Leverage is moderate, with a debt‑to‑equity ratio of [[V.ratio.debt_to_equity]] times, suggesting a balanced financing mix. Free cash flow of [[V.ratio.free_cash_flow]] dollars demonstrates ample cash generation to fund share repurchases and dividends. The annual‑filing price‑to‑earnings multiple is [[V.ratio.price_earnings]] times, reflecting market expectations of continued growth.

insight.text: The leverage level indicated by the debt‑to‑equity ratio is a key gauge of balance‑sheet risk.
